# input: # Hindi's separators are English's — comma for groups, point for the decimal —
# so only the grouping *rule* separates the two, and only on the way out.
# Reading is grouping-agnostic: `parseNumber` strips the separator wherever it
# falls, so the Indian form below and the international one on the next line
# Writing is not. `formatNumber` groups in fixed periods of three and
# `NumberFormatSpec` carries no grouping rule, so this engine prints
# "1,234,567" where a Hindi page writes "12,34,567". Recorded rather than
# worked around — the same gap `core/src/locale/hi.ts` documents at length,
# and the row that will change the day core learns about grouping periods.
# लाख is read as a magnitude word and lands on 100000; only its printed
# grouping is subject to the gap above.
# फुट / फीट, the only unit here whose number axis moves: Hindi borrowed the
# English singular and plural as two separate words. The other seven are
# consonant-final masculine loans that do not inflect after a numeral.
# The operators are bare words, and a conversion is a postposition *after* the
# target rather than a preposition before it — में, को and से all mark it.
